-74.03010,40.96340.name: Fertility Institute of New Jersey and New York
-74.03010,40.96340.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Zalman Levine, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

137.94681,34.88927.name: Fuji Research Park (FRP) and Tokyo Research Park (TRP)
137.94681,34.88927.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Kyowa Kirin Co., Ltd.. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-2.59982,51.45197.name: CREATE Fertility Bristol
-2.59982,51.45197.state: 1 Trinity Street, College Green, Bristol, BS1 5TE
-2.59982,51.45197.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

5.06000,52.64000.name: Hendrix Genetics
5.06000,52.64000.desc: A Dutch multi-species animal breeding company — poultry, pigs, aquaculture, turkeys. A handful of breeding companies supply the genetics for most of the world’s farmed animals, so a trait selected here reaches enormous populations within a few generations.

-122.14300,37.44190.name: a16z Bio + Health
-122.14300,37.44190.desc: The biology arm of a large venture firm, funding companies across editing, synthetic biology and health software. Venture capital decides which of these technologies gets built before any regulator sees them, on a return horizon of seven to ten years — which favours products with a clear buyer and a short path, and disfavours anything whose value shows up as harm avoided.

-122.14300,37.44190.name: Verily / Debug — automated rearing systems
-122.14300,37.44190.desc: Automated mass-rearing, sorting and release systems for sterile mosquitoes, built by a technology company. When releasing tens of millions of insects becomes a logistics problem, the remaining constraint is permission — and permission systems were designed when rearing capacity was the brake.

117.17000,39.10800.name: Tianjin Biosecurity Guidelines for Codes of Conduct for Scientists
117.17000,39.10800.state: Tianjin — Tianjin University Center for Biosafety Research and Strategy
117.17000,39.10800.desc: Ten guiding principles for responsible conduct in the life sciences, agreed between Chinese and international academies in 2021 and endorsed by the InterAcademy Partnership. They carry no force at all. Their significance is where they came from: a code of conduct for dual-use research negotiated with Chinese institutions is a rarer thing than another Western guideline.

139.76490,35.67620.name: Nippon Paper Industries
139.76490,35.67620.desc: One of the Japanese paper manufacturers that pursued engineered eucalyptus for pulping rather than for yield or pest resistance: its research aimed at blocking genes controlling stages of lignin synthesis, producing trees with less lignin and more cellulose. Competitors pursued the same end by different routes, one targeting lower lignin content directly and another making lignin easier to remove during processing so that less bleaching agent is needed. The distinction is worth holding: the crop side of this map is dominated by traits that change what happens in the FIELD, and this is a trait designed to change what happens in the MILL. A tree engineered to be easier to dissolve is a different proposition from one engineered to resist an insect, and the plantations these companies hold sit in Papua New Guinea, New Zealand, Australia and Viet Nam rather than in Japan.
